name: Fitness Tracker
highLevelGoals: The user aims to easily record and monitor various physical activities, such as running, walking, or cycling, to maintain a comprehensive log of their exercise habits.
The user seeks clear and intuitive visual representations of their activity data to easily monitor their fitness progress, identify trends, and stay motivated.
The user desires the ability to set, edit, and track personalized fitness goals (e.g., daily steps, calories burned) to provide clear targets and maintain focus on their fitness journey.
The user expects to receive personalized workout recommendations and plans based on their fitness level, preferences, and goals to maximize the effectiveness of their workouts.
The user aims for the application to connect and automatically sync data from their wearable devices to ensure accurate and up-to-date tracking of their fitness metrics.
The user wants to share their fitness activities, achievements, and progress on social media to engage with friends, celebrate milestones, and inspire others.
The wearable device aims to accurately collect and transmit fitness data, such as heart rate, steps, and calories burned, to the application in real-time.
The wearable device seeks to establish and maintain a stable connection with the fitness application to ensure continuous and uninterrupted data synchronization.
lowLevelGoals: The user can initiate the recording of a new physical activity (e.g., running, walking, cycling) within the application.
The user can terminate the recording of a physical activity within the application.
The user can input details for a physical activity that was not tracked in real-time, including activity type, duration, and intensity.
The user can access a chronological list of all their tracked and manually logged physical activities.
The user can view a summary of their physical activities for a specific day, including total duration, calories burned, and distance covered.
The user can view graphical representations of their activity trends over a week, showing changes in performance metrics.
The user can access charts illustrating their progress for specific fitness metrics (e.g., average pace, total steps) on a monthly basis.
The user receives an alert or notification when they achieve a predefined fitness milestone (e.g., 100km run, 10,000 steps daily for a week).
The user can define a new fitness goal, specifying the metric (e.g., daily steps), target value, and timeframe.
The user can modify the parameters (e.g., target value, timeframe) of an already established fitness goal.
The user can indicate that a specific fitness goal has been achieved.
The user can see their current progress against all active fitness goals.
The user can initiate the generation of a workout plan based on their specified fitness level, preferences, and goals.
The user can access a list of recommended exercises or activities for the current day.
The user can modify their preferences (e.g., intensity, duration, exercise types) to influence future workout recommendations.
The user can provide feedback on the perceived difficulty of a completed workout to help refine future recommendations.
The user can start the process of connecting the application with a new compatible wearable device.
The user can see a list of all wearable devices currently paired with the application.
The user can force the application to sync the latest data from a connected wearable device.
The user can post details of a specific completed activity (e.g., run, cycle) to their chosen social media platform.
The user can post an announcement of achieving a fitness goal to their chosen social media platform.
The user can configure which data points are shared and to which platforms when sharing fitness achievements.
The wearable device sends continuous heart rate measurements to the connected fitness application.
The wearable device sends continuous step count measurements to the connected fitness application.
The wearable device sends continuous estimated calorie burn measurements to the connected fitness application.
The wearable device initiates and maintains a stable BLE connection for data transfer with the fitness application.
The wearable device attempts to re-establish a connection with the fitness application if the connection is lost.
The wearable device provides visual or haptic feedback to the user regarding its connection status with the application.
